nodes.rationale: Sticky footer shows '7 selected, 11.4 GB' and an orange Delete selected button, keeping the destructive action visually distinct.

nodes.norm_label: drive free space meters (c:, d:, f:)
nodes.rationale: Header shows per-drive free space bars so users see disk pressure before and after cleaning.

nodes.label: Filter, Select Unused For N Days, Clear Selection
nodes.norm_label: filter, select unused for n days, clear selection
nodes.rationale: Path/type filter plus age-based bulk selection (30 days) targets stale artifacts while sparing recently used ones.

nodes.label: Last Changed Age Highlight
nodes.rationale: Recently changed items (e.g. '3 days ago') are highlighted in amber as a caution signal.

nodes.label: DevSweep Main Window (dark theme)
nodes.rationale: Single-window dark UI with tagline 'Removes build output and package caches that your tools can rebuild', framing the app as a safe cleaner of regenerable artifacts.

nodes.label: Project Folders / Global Caches Tabs
nodes.rationale: Results split into project-local artifacts (14 items, 17.1 GB) and global caches (5 items, 2.9 GB), each tab showing count and total size.

nodes.label: Running Process Lock Banner
nodes.rationale: Warning 'Running now: node. Folders they use are locked.' prevents deleting folders in use by live developer processes.

nodes.label: Scan Results Table
nodes.rationale: Sorted by size descending with inline size bars; columns Size, Folder (name, project, full path), Type, Last changed, How it comes back, plus an open-folder action.

nodes.label: Where to Look (scan roots) Panel
nodes.rationale: Folder chips (e.g. D:\devsweep-demo) with an Add folder button let users pick scan roots.

nodes.label: How It Comes Back Recovery Badges
nodes.norm_label: how it comes back recovery badges
nodes.rationale: Each row is classified as 'Rebuilds on its own' (green), 'Needs reinstall' (amber) or 'Check first' (orange) with the rebuild command shown (cargo build, npm install, python -m venv, cmake -B build, flutter build, next build), so users understand the cost of deleting.

nodes.norm_label: chown command hint for root-owned folders (linux)

nodes.label: Permanent deletion (no Recycle Bin)
nodes.rationale: Moving 50 GB of node_modules to the Recycle Bin or Trash frees nothing.

nodes.label: Reports real free-space change
nodes.community_name: Step 03 Delete (still owned and unused, no links, real space freed)
nodes.rationale: pnpm and Cargo hard links make counted size overstate what deletion frees, so the report shows the change in free disk space next to the counted size.

nodes.label: Runs as normal user, never self-elevates
nodes.norm_label: runs as normal user, never self-elevates
nodes.rationale: Access-denied folders usually come from admin terminals or sudo; Windows offers an explicit Restart as administrator via UAC with the same rules, Linux shows a chown command instead of running as root.

nodes.label: Fixed scanner exclusion list
nodes.community_name: Project folder ownership rule (project file next to it, marker inside)
nodes.rationale: Scanner never enters Program Files, AppData, .git, editor and toolchain folders, game libraries, resources folders (installed Electron apps ship node_modules + package.json there), and on Linux system folders, ~/.config, ~/.cache, ~/.local, Flatpak, Snap, Wine and Node version managers, where installed tools look like projects.

nodes.label: In-use folder locking
nodes.community_name: Project folder ownership rule (project file next to it, marker inside)
nodes.rationale: A folder can't be selected when a program runs from it or a dev tool's working folder is inside the project; caches lock while their package manager runs. On Linux only the user's own processes are visible.

nodes.label: Project folder ownership rule (project file next to it, marker inside)
nodes.community_name: Project folder ownership rule (project file next to it, marker inside)
nodes.norm_label: project folder ownership rule (project file next to it, marker inside)
nodes.rationale: A folder only counts when its owning project file sits next to it; ambiguous names like build, target and bin also require a file the build tool writes inside, so user folders with the same name are never offered.

nodes.label: Why DevSweep: rebuildable build output piles up
nodes.norm_label: why devsweep: rebuildable build output piles up

nodes.label: Global package caches cleaning
nodes.rationale: Caches live at fixed paths in the user folder; DevSweep empties the cache folder but keeps the folder itself, and runs pnpm store prune for the pnpm store so only unused packages are removed.
